name: London Buddhist Centre
summary: A Buddhist centre on Roman Road, E2, that teaches meditation and Buddhism, runs yoga classes every day and holds retreats at its centre in Suffolk.
crowd: The centre says taking part does not depend on being a Buddhist, and that most of its events suit people new to meditation or Buddhism.

cost.notes: Regular classes are free of charge; retreats ask for payment when you book.

story.opened: Opened in 1978 inside Bethnal Green's old fire station, according to Londonist.
story.then: Londonist says the building was put up as a fire station in 1889 and had stood disused since 1968, before the centre moved in.
story.now: The venue's own website says the centre hosts Buddhist festivals, daily yoga, family events, PoetryEast evenings with well-known artists and school visits, and runs two charity shops. It is open Monday to Saturday, 10am to 5pm, and some events are also online.
worth_knowing: The building was a fire station from 1889 until 1968, according to Londonist.
Its Lama's Pyjamas charity shop is run on Buddhist ethical principles, says the venue's own website.
